title: Getting a table game onto a table
target: How to stock, place and keep the tabletop games in TCG Card Shop Simulator: what a game set is made of, how it restocks, and what the shop's own list decides about what is on show.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A table or game area that customers can reach
A licence or space for tabletop goods
Shelf or table space for what arrives

steps.do: Order tabletop games through their own screen rather than the item screen, because they restock apart from items and cards.
steps.because: tabletop games restock through a screen of their own (RestockItemBoardGameScreen)

steps.do: Treat a game as a set rather than a single product, because the game keeps a tabletop game as a set with a record of its own.
steps.because: a tabletop game is kept as a set with its own record (TableGameItemSet, TableGameItemSetData)

steps.do: Check that every part of a set arrived, because the game names them: a play mat, a deck box and a comic book.
steps.because: a set has named parts (playMatType, deckBoxType, comicBookType)

steps.do: Expect the parts to be visible in the world, because each of them has a mesh of its own.
steps.because: each part has its own mesh (m_DeckBoxMesh, m_ComicBookMesh, m_PlayMatMesh)

steps.do: Put the table where a customer can reach it, because customers have states for wanting to play and for walking to a table.
steps.because: customers have states for wanting to play, walking to the play table and playing there (WantToPlayGame, WalkToPlayTable, PlayingAtTable)

steps.do: Let the shop's own list decide what is on show rather than putting everything out, because the shop data holds which board game kinds are shown.
steps.because: the shop data holds which board game item kinds are shown (m_ShownBoardGameItemType)

steps.do: Use the shipped icons when telling one game from another, because the game has icons for particular tabletop games.
steps.because: the game ships icons for particular tabletop games (Icon_Boardgame_Speedrobo_Necro, Icon_Boardgame_Speedrobo_Mafia)

steps.do: Do not confuse a tabletop game with the playable card game, because playable card sets are defined separately.
steps.because: playable card sets are defined by the game of their own (PlayCardSet, PlayCardSetUI)

steps.do: Reorder before the shelf is empty, because the same board game screen is the one that brings them back.
steps.because: the board game restock screen is the one these goods use (RestockItemBoardGameScreen)

commonMistakes: Trying to restock a tabletop game from the item screen and finding nothing there.
Treating a game set as one product and being surprised by the play mat, deck box and comic book.
Putting a table out of reach and expecting customers to use it.
Mixing up the tabletop games you sell with the card game customers play.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
